info.title: krabshell API
info.summary: Drive and watch a krabshell simulation over HTTP.
info.description:
The REST and WebSocket surface of krabshell (spec §9). Every route reads the driver's published view or posts a message to it, so no request can cost the simulation a tick.

Errors are `application/problem+json` bodies with a stable `code` to switch on. Everything but `/health` and this document needs the dashboard token, given as a bearer header, a `krabshell_token` cookie, or `?token=` (the only way a browser WebSocket can send it). A server started without `DASHBOARD_TOKEN` accepts every request.

A request the server cannot parse (a missing or malformed query parameter, a body that is not the JSON the route takes, a missing `Content-Type`) is refused before it reaches a handler, with a plain-text 400, 415 or 422 rather than a problem body.

get.description: Unauthenticated on purpose, so a process monitor can watch the driver without holding the token. 503 when the tick thread has died or the model has faulted.

503.description: The driver is dead or faulted. The body says which.

get.description: The OpenAPI description of this API, for Swagger UI, Redoc, client generators and the like. Unauthenticated.
What is loaded, what it is doing, and how fast.

post.description: Run continuously. With no body, or `target_tps` null, as fast as the machine allows.
Advance `n` ticks (1 with no body), then pause. Answers once the burst has finished, so the status describes the world after it. A burst still going after 10 seconds is answered with mode `stepping`.
Rebuild the loaded scenario from tick 0, paused.
Change the target rate without starting or pausing.

200.description: Every pack in the scenario directory.

post.description: Upload a zipped pack. The id is the `id` field, or the archive's filename without its extension. Size and entry limits are enforced while the archive is read (spec §13).

pack.description: The zip. A part named `file` is accepted too.

id.description: What to call the pack. Defaults to the archive's filename stem.

post.description: Replace the running world with this pack, paused at tick 0.

200.description: The config the driver is running with.

put.description: Validated, then applied. Changing some fields (resolution, root, parallelism, model parameters) rebuilds the world; `reset_fields` names them.

get.description: The config as it is currently effective, not the file on disk (spec §10.2), as `<scenario>-config.toml`.
The objects in some cells. Name the cells with `cells`, or a disk with `center` and `k`; with neither, every published cell, which is refused once the world has more than 20 000 occupied cells.

parameters.name: center
parameters.description: Centre of a disk of cells. Ignored when `cells` is given.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Rings around `center`. Values above 64 are treated as 64.

parameters.name: res
parameters.description: Accepted and ignored. Use `/state/map` to aggregate.

200.description: The cells asked for that have anything in them.

get.description: Occupancy rolled up to a display resolution, each cell with its boundary ready to draw (spec §7.3).

parameters.name: res
parameters.description: Resolution to aggregate to. Defaults to the config's `view_resolution`; clamped to between 0 and the occupancy resolution.

get.description: Every object with an exact position, for drawing individual things rather than cell counts. The headers carry the tick, the tick length and the run mode, so a client can predict motion between polls.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Comma-separated kinds to include. Omit for every kind.

get.description: What the model publishes beside its agents, as it publishes it. For the drones: geofences, open orders, stations, regions of interest and courier range. Null for a model with none.
The committed world, copied out of the driver, as `<scenario>-tick<n>.ckpt.json`.

post.description: Replace the world with a checkpoint. Pause first. A gold-profile checkpoint whose hash does not match its cells is refused.

get.description: The objects in one cell; an empty list if there are none. 404 only when the cell is empty and the published view was capped, so it may have been dropped.

post.description: Hand one intent to the driver and wait up to half a second for it to be applied. A paused world will not reach it: it stays queued, and the answer says `queued`. The WebSocket is the better path for anything interactive. Bodies are capped at 16 KiB, and each actor's submission rate is limited.

get.description: Every intent applied since load, one JSON object per line, as `<scenario>-tick<n>.intents.jsonl`. Kept only in the gold profile (spec §8.4).
Gauges in the Prometheus text exposition format, each named `krabshell_*`.

text/plain.example:
# HELP krabshell_tick Committed tick.
# TYPE krabshell_tick gauge
krabshell_tick 1200

get.description: Sightings, waypoints, deliveries, breaches and the like, newer than `since`. The driver keeps the latest few hundred; a caller that falls further behind sees a gap between its `since` and the first `seq` returned.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only reports with a larger `seq`. Pass back the last answer's `last_seq`.

get.description: Compile a coordinate to an A5 cell, with its shape and whether intents may address it (spec §7.2).

parameters.name: res
parameters.description: Resolution. Defaults to the occupancy resolution.

get.description: Fences open now, waiting to open, and closed lately, with the latest breach and reroute reports. Empty for a model without geofences.

post.description: A circle or a polygon, in degrees, with an optional name, lifetime, delay and altitude band.

delete.description: Close an open fence, whoever opened it, or cancel one waiting to open. From the next tick.

patch.description: Open, waiting to open, or previously closed. From the next tick.

post.summary: Change how long a geofence stays open

get.description: The stations, how busy they are, how far the couriers can reach by way of them, and the latest station reports. Empty, and not `available`, for a model without stations.

delete.description: Whoever added it. From the next tick.

get.description: The regions, the surveys done, the drones assigned, and the latest region and survey reports. Empty, and not `available`, for a model without them.

post.description: For the drones to survey. From the next tick.

delete.description: Whoever designated it, a crash included. From the next tick.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket (spec §9.3). The server sends `hello`, then a `snapshot` and `delta`s for the cells the client subscribes to, at most `publish_hz` times a second, plus a `tick` with the metrics. Clients send `ClientMessage`s and receive `ServerMessage`s, as JSON text frames. Browsers cannot set headers on a WebSocket, so pass the token as `?token=`.

101.description: Switching to the WebSocket protocol. Messages are `ClientMessage` up and `ServerMessage` down.

cookie.name: krabshell_token
cookie.description: Set by the dashboard's login form.

query.name: token
query.description: For WebSockets, which cannot carry a header from a browser.

Id.name: id
Id.description: The id the list gives it.

SimTick.description: The tick the body is from.

SimMode.description: The run mode when the body was read.

SimTickSeconds.description: Simulated seconds per tick, when the model says.

RunStatus.description: The run status, after the command if there was one.

IntentAccepted.description: Applied, or queued for the next tick.

BadRequest.description: The request, or the intent it made, was refused. `code` says why.

Unauthorized.description: No token, or the wrong one.

Conflict.description: Not in this run mode: `requires_pause` or `requires_reset`.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is over the limit.

TooManyRequests.description: `rate_limited` (this actor) or `backpressured` (the driver's queue is full).

DriverUnavailable.description: The simulation thread is not running, or did not answer in time.

meta.description: Anything more the code carries, such as a rejected intent's reason.

ErrorCode.description: Stable error codes. Switch on these, not on `detail`.

GeoCell.description: An A5 cell id, as 16 hex digits. Inputs may also be `0x`-prefixed hex or a decimal u64.

Profile.description: `gold`: sequential, seeded and hashable, for science and replay. `fast`: parallel allowed, for games and visualisation.

last_publish_age_ms.description: How long since the last published view.

truncated_cells.description: Cells left out of the published view at the cap.

root.description: The island root. Absent for a global grid.

hash.description: Stable hash of the cells, in the gold profile.

IntentRecord.description: One line of the recent intent activity.

rejected.description: Null when applied; the rejection code otherwise.

target_tps.description: Null means as fast as possible.

truncated.description: The published view dropped cells at the cap.

target_tps.description: Ticks per second to aim for. Absent or null: as fast as possible.
Ticks per second to aim for. Null: as fast as possible.

seed_agents.description: Agents the pack places itself, before the model adds any.

parallel.description: krABMaga's parallel schedule. Changing it rebuilds the world.

publish_hz.description: Upper bound on views published per second.

intent_horizon.description: How many ticks ahead an intent may be scheduled.

max_published_cells.description: Cap on cells in one published view.

intent_rate_per_actor.description: Sustained intents per second per actor; bursts of twice this are allowed.

auto_recover.description: Restart the driver after a tick panic.

root.description: Island root. Absent: a global grid.

view_resolution.description: The coarser resolution the dashboard map aggregates to.

Config.description: Every section is optional on input and filled with defaults. Unknown fields are refused.

model.description: Passed to the model on reset.

reset_fields.description: Fields whose change rebuilt the world.

state.description: Whatever the model keeps for this kind.

truncated.description: The published view was capped, so cells may be missing.

activity.description: What a drone's behaviour is doing: delivering, surveying, charging and so on.

Checkpoint.description: The committed world. In the gold profile, `meta.hash` is checked against the cells on restore.

fields.description: Model state that is not agents.

IntentVerb.description: What to do. A model's own verbs are `{"custom": code}`.

id.description: Chosen by the client. A repeat is refused as a duplicate.

tick.description: Tick to apply at. Absent: the next one.

cell.description: Where it applies, at the occupancy resolution, inside the world.

agent.description: The agent it is about, if any.

actor.description: Who sent it. Rate limits are per actor.

tick.description: The tick it was applied at.

status.description: `queued` when the world did not reach it within half a second, as when paused. A queued intent the model later refuses shows up in the list's `refused`.

Report.description: Something the model saw or did.

uid.description: Stable id, used as the CoT uid.

last_seq.description: The highest `seq` so far. Pass it back as `since`.

Refused.description: An intent the model refused lately, so a client that was told `queued` learns why it never took effect.

Fence.description: A geofence, as the model publishes it. A circle has `lat_e7`, `lon_e7` and `radius_m`; a polygon has `points`.

floor_m.description: Metres above ground. Absent: from the surface.

opened_tick.description: For a scheduled fence, when it will open.

breaches.description: Open fences only: breaches in the recent reports.

tick_seconds.description: Simulated seconds per tick, when the model says.

rev.description: Bumped whenever a fence opens or closes.

margin_m.description: How far the simulated drones keep from a fence.

recent.description: Latest breach and reroute reports, newest first.

minutes.description: How long it stays open. -1 or absent: until closed.

after_minutes.description: Delay before it opens. 0 or absent: the next tick.

floor_m.description: Metres above ground. Absent or null: from the surface.

ceiling_m.description: Metres above ground, above the floor. Absent or null: unlimited.

minutes.description: Minutes from now it stays open, or -1 until closed.

slots.description: Drones that can be down on it, or coming down onto it, at once.

drones.description: On the ground at it now.

waiting.description: Drones holding off for a slot.

available.description: The model publishes stations at all.

range.description: How far each hub's couriers can deliver by way of the stations, as the model publishes it.

source.description: `scenario`, `dashboard`, `intent`, or `crash` for one left where a drone fell.

assigned.description: Drones on their way to survey it.

available.description: The model publishes regions of interest at all.

recent.description: Latest region and survey reports, newest first.

in_world.description: Intents may address this cell in the current run.

edge_meters.description: Nominal edge length at this resolution.

objects.description: Agents that left. Absent: the whole cell emptied.

oneOf.title: set_aoi
oneOf.description: Replace the area of interest with a disk of `k` rings, at most 64.

ServerMessage.description: Server to client, over `/ws`. Protocol version 1.

oneOf.title: delta
oneOf.description: What changed in the subscribed cells since the last frame.

oneOf.title: rejected
oneOf.description: `reason` is one of `stale`, `too_far`, `backpressured`, `duplicate`, `out_of_bounds`, `rejected` or `rate_limited`, with its fields beside it.
